tasks.short: Prepare the HR operating budget, agree spending priorities, and monitor costs against the approved plan.

steps.what: Retrieve HR spending and commitments from the {ERP}.
Collect staffing, recruitment, training, and supplier spending proposals.
Calculate baseline costs and alternative spending scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Negotiate service priorities and affordable spending with the finance team and department managers.
Approve the HR budget and spending limits.
Record approved budget lines and limits in the {ERP}.
Compare actual spending with budget and decide corrective action.

tasks.design: Use {WORKFLOW} forms to collect proposals and a scheduled {DATA_PLATFORM} job to join approved inputs with {ERP} actuals. Deterministic calculations generate scenarios and a {BI} variance dashboard; approval precedes budget posting to the {ERP}. The HR manager negotiates priorities and recommends corrective action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost mappings, proposal formats, and planning assumptions differed across teams. Existing reporting often covered actuals without commitments or service demand.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and reporting can cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building mappings, scenario calculations, and validation checks; no model loop is required.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing affordable service levels and estimating recruitment or training demand remain uncertain. Poor commitment data can make an apparently precise forecast misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The HR manager explains the consequences of cuts and negotiates tradeoffs between employee needs and available funds.

ambition.what: Monthly recruitment-versus-training spending recommendations using current commitments.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less consolidation and more discussion of service demand and spending choices. Budget approval rights stay unchanged; any delegated reallocation limit needs agreement with the finance director.

reach.task: Cost a training plan against delivery capacity.
reach.learn: Course unit costs, attendance assumptions, and how training outcomes support investment choices.

reach.task: Estimate the cost of proposed benefit changes.
reach.learn: Eligibility rules, employer contributions, and uncertainty in employee uptake.

evidence.claim: Structured budget inputs support deterministic scenario calculations and variance reporting; the proposed scope and effort are estimates.
Observed chatbot adoption does not establish large reductions in HR working hours.

assumptions: The task covers HR operating costs; payroll totals may be planning inputs.
Step shares and remaining time are estimates for a mid-size European company, not measured savings.
Existing reporting and form capabilities are used before custom code.
Build ranges cover an initial implementation with reusable shared components and are not additive across tasks.
Access should use aggregated cost data where employee-level detail is unnecessary.
unknowns: Whether HR controls payroll expenditure or only its own operating budget.
Available interfaces, licences, cost mappings, and commitment data.
Current approval thresholds and reallocation authority.
Countries involved and whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed data use.
research_questions: Can existing budget functionality calculate scenarios and track commitments?
Which cost categories most often cause forecast errors?
Would aggregated planning inputs remove the need for employee-level access?
new_work: Maintain cost mappings and planning assumptions.
Resolve missing commitments and late proposals.
Review scenario totals and unexpected variances.
Monitor imports and prevent duplicate budget postings.

tasks.short: Maintain personnel records and report hires, transfers, appraisal completion, and absence trends.

steps.what: Enter approved employee changes and absence records in the {HCM}.
Export workforce movements and absence totals from the {HCM}.
Export hire records from the {ATS}.
Export appraisal completion records from the {TALENT}.
Join exports and resolve duplicate employees, missing dates, and conflicting totals.
Calculate workforce measures and assemble charts in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Check report totals and disclosure risks before releasing the workforce report.

tasks.design: Configure approved change forms and validation in the {HCM}, and scheduled exports from the {HCM}, {ATS}, and {TALENT}. A deterministic {DATA_PLATFORM} pipeline reconciles employee identifiers and feeds defined measures to {BI}, with restricted access and suppression of small groups. The HR manager resolves disputed records and approves report release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different identifiers, effective dates, and metric definitions made exports difficult to reconcile. Manual handling often substituted for agreed data ownership.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record workflows and reporting can handle the main task. AI-assisted coding can speed up connectors and reconciliation checks without interpreting employee data through a model.
tasks.still_hard: Historical corrections, disputed absence records, and meaningful denominators need accountable owners. Small teams can remain identifiable even in aggregated reports.
tasks.human_edge: The HR manager distinguishes a data defect from a real workforce issue and challenges misleading comparisons.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of departments needing an absence-support discussion.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from export repair to investigating exceptions and explaining workforce trends. The HR manager can prioritise support discussions; employment decisions still follow existing authority.

reach.learn: Effective dates, evidence requirements, and when a correction needs escalation.
Cutoff dates, absence codes, and differences between HR and payroll reporting periods.

evidence.claim: Approved record updates, scheduled exports, and defined statistical measures generally support deterministic automation.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on people.
In the Netherlands, specified staff-data and monitoring arrangements can require works-council consent, subject to statutory exceptions.

assumptions: Reports describe workforce movements and completion rates; they do not generate employee performance scores.
Approved changes have structured fields and supporting evidence.
Step shares and remaining time are estimates, including exception review.
GDPR applies; access, purpose, retention, and special-category data handling need appropriate controls.
Consultation and access ranges allow initial preparation; formal national procedures may take longer.
Shared data components can also support the budgeting and coordination tasks.
unknowns: Whether employee identifiers match across systems.
Which absence data contains health information and who may access it.
Agreed metric definitions, recipients, and minimum reporting group sizes.
Historical error rates and owners of disputed records.
Countries involved and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can native reporting supply the required measures without a separate pipeline?
Which reconciliation errors require human evidence rather than a mapping rule?
How should reports prevent identification through small groups or repeated filtering?
new_work: Resolve quarantined records and disputed source values.
Maintain identifiers, metric definitions, and access rules.
Review disclosure risks when adding dimensions or recipients.
Monitor failed imports and changes to source schemas.

tasks.short: Explain policies, job conditions, pay, progression, and benefits to employees and candidates.

steps.what: Receive the question and establish the employee or candidate context.
Find current policies, benefit terms, and job information in the {DOCS}.
Check authorised personal eligibility and employment terms in the {HCM}.
Draft an explanation linking the question to applicable policy and eligibility facts.

loop.input: HR inquiry, approved policy passages, and minimum authorised eligibility facts.
loop.output: HR answer draft with passage citations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate cited passages, policy versions, and eligibility fields; an HR specialist checks applicability before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one repair; missing, conflicting, or unsupported terms route to an HR specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard questions. Novel free-text questions spanning several policies need a bounded drafting loop.

steps.what: Discuss sensitive circumstances, policy ambiguity, or progression expectations with the requester.
Check and send the written answer, recording any follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure an inquiry queue in {HELPDESK} and searchable, versioned policy references in {DOCS}, with authorised eligibility lookups from {HCM}. Approved FAQ answers use templates; a bounded loop drafts unusual answers with citations for HR review before sending through {EMAIL}. Sensitive questions retain a direct conversation and a visible route to an HR specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were scattered, ownership was unclear, and personalised answers required checking several sources. Search alone did not explain how terms applied to a particular question.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned knowledge articles and structured eligibility checks support reliable retrieval. A small drafting loop can reduce writing effort once source quality and access are settled.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting policies, collective agreements, personal circumstances, and implied promises about pay or promotion need human interpretation. Keeping source material current remains ongoing work.
tasks.human_edge: HR recognises the concern behind the question and explains difficult limits without losing trust.

ambition.what: Provide shift workers with an out-of-hours policy reference service and a tracked human callback.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer repeated searches and more complex advice and follow-up. HR gains a clearer view of recurring policy confusion, while authority to grant exceptions stays unchanged.

reach.role: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialist
reach.task: Explain benefit eligibility and job-level criteria.
reach.learn: Benefit exclusions, job-evaluation criteria, and when a written answer could create an unintended commitment.
Collective-agreement precedence, escalation thresholds, and national employment rules.

evidence.claim: Versioned policy retrieval, eligibility rules, and bounded answer drafting support an HR answer desk; proposed effort and savings are estimates.
The reported AskHR case includes a first-year HR NPS decline when access to HR partners and the phone line changed.
GDPR Article 22 supports keeping significant employment decisions outside solely automated answer handling.

assumptions: Approved policy material has an owner, version, effective date, and scope.
Candidates receive public information and authorised offer terms, not employee records.
Standard FAQs can bypass model drafting through approved templates.
The model drafts explanations; it does not decide eligibility exceptions, pay, promotion, or employment rights.
Step shares give substantial weight to conversations despite the weaker mailbox prior.
GDPR applies; consultation requirements depend on national rules and the actual deployment.
unknowns: Question volumes, languages, shift patterns, and existing human support routes.
Policy completeness and conflicts with contracts or collective agreements.
Which eligibility fields may be exposed to each requester.
National consultation obligations and approved data-processing arrangements.
Whether existing search and templates cover most questions.
research_questions: What proportion of questions can an approved FAQ answer directly?
Which question types must always route to a specialist?
Can a representative test set verify citations, policy scope, and refusal to invent terms?
How will employees find and use the human callback route?
new_work: Maintain policy versions, FAQ templates, and escalation routes.
Handle unsupported questions and eligibility conflicts.
Sample answers for incorrect citations and unintended promises.
Review inquiry trends without exposing individual concerns.

tasks.short: Set HR priorities, coordinate personnel and training work, and direct labor-relations activity.

steps.what: Collect recruitment, staffing, training, and employee-relations status from responsible specialists.
Review deadlines, service demand, capacity, and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Agree priorities and service tradeoffs with department managers and the HR team.
Assign approved actions, owners, deadlines, and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Coordinate training delivery and resolve conflicts with operational managers.
Discuss labor-relations issues with employee representatives and agree next steps within delegated authority.
Chase outstanding actions and update delivery status.

tasks.design: Configure an HR delivery register, ownership rules, dependencies, and reminders in {PROJECT} and {WORKFLOW}. Feed approved aggregate measures from {HCM}, {ATS}, and {LMS} into {BI}, while keeping sensitive employee-relations details in a restricted {HELPDESK} queue. The HR manager sets priorities, approves assignments, and conducts operational and labor-relations discussions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates lived in separate team queues and messages. Managers needed a shared view without exposing confidential case details.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing work-management configuration can handle ownership, deadlines, and reminders. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting aggregate status feeds; the coordination process needs no autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Capacity estimates, conflicting priorities, negotiations, and emerging employee concerns resist fixed rules. Recorded status can lag behind what specialists know.
tasks.human_edge: The HR manager builds agreement, recognises tension, and changes priorities when the formal plan no longer fits reality.

ambition.what: Weekly redeployment of HR service capacity between recruitment administration and training coordination.

tasks.altitude: The week has less status chasing and more capacity decisions, coaching, and negotiation. Within existing authority, the HR manager can adjust service assignments more frequently; employment allocation and major commitments retain their separate approval routes.

reach.task: Coordinate a quarterly training delivery portfolio.
reach.learn: Delivery capacity, operational release constraints, and evidence of training effectiveness.

reach.task: Prepare and track an employee-representative consultation.
reach.learn: Consultation timing, negotiating mandates, confidentiality, and national procedural rules.

reach.task: Balance an HR service queue against available capacity.
reach.learn: Service-level definitions, demand estimation, and escalation of employee-impacting decisions.

evidence.claim: Registers, deadlines, ownership fields, and reminders support deterministic HR coordination, while priorities and negotiations remain human.
The EU AI Act identifies specified employment-related AI uses, including allocation and performance evaluation, as high-risk categories.
Article 26 includes worker and representative information duties for applicable workplace high-risk AI deployments.
The documented multi-occupation study found limited working-hour effects from chatbot adoption, including occupations in HR.

assumptions: Assignment automation records human-approved service plans and does not rank employees or infer performance.
General delivery dashboards expose restricted case status only as authorised aggregate counts.
All priority and negotiation decisions remain within existing delegated authority.
Step shares reflect substantial human coordination; broad automation probabilities do not imply automating those conversations.
GDPR applies throughout; national consultation and employment rules vary.
EU AI Act classification and applicable dates must be checked if predictive allocation or employee scoring enters scope.
Build ranges cover an initial implementation; formal consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Current delegation limits, team structure, and service ownership.
Reliable capacity measures and whether staff already maintain a shared delivery register.
Who may see sensitive employee-relations status.
Countries involved, representative arrangements, and required consultation procedures.
Available interfaces and whether the intended deployment includes regulated employment AI uses.
research_questions: Which status feeds can be shared as aggregates without exposing cases?
Can existing work-management features cover the whole initial scope?
Which assignment decisions need separate approval because they affect employment terms or workload?
What current EU AI Act obligations and national procedures apply to any later scoring or allocation features?
new_work: Maintain service definitions, ownership, and escalation thresholds.
Resolve stale status feeds and disputed capacity estimates.
Review reminder volume and suppress unhelpful notifications.
Maintain restricted access and separate general delivery status from confidential case records.

role.altitude: The HR manager spends less time assembling reports, budgets, answers, and status updates, and more time interpreting workforce needs, coaching specialists, and negotiating decisions. Existing approval rights remain; broader spending or employment authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Cost training and benefit proposals with adjacent specialists.
Connect absence reporting with payroll reconciliation.
Prepare consultation briefs and track commitments with a labor relations specialist.
Manage HR service capacity using demand and delivery evidence.
skills_to_grow: Define workforce measures and recognise misleading comparisons.
Model costs, commitments, and service-capacity scenarios.
Set access boundaries and maintain reliable policy sources.
Review cited drafts and resolve data exceptions.
Negotiate priorities and explain employee-impacting tradeoffs.
Distinguish administrative automation from regulated employment decision support.
role.ambitious_version: Run a monthly workforce-and-service review that connects HR costs, recruitment demand, training delivery, and employee concerns, producing named recommendations and tracking their outcomes.
